children.title: 3/26- Sharecropping
Sharecropping Simulation Questions
children.content:
Questions to consider and then answer at the end of the simulation:

  1. Upon signing your contract with the landlord, how did you expect the game to play out? Identify possible similarities and differences between the game and the reality of sharecropping.

  2. Based on your experience with the game, do you think sharecroppers had a reasonable opportunity to better their situation? Justify your position.

  3. Do you think the landlord’s power over you is fair? What do you think it means for someone to have a “fair” chance to achieve economic success?

  4. Compare and contrast sharecropping with slavery as a form of economic organization.

  5. Assess sharecropping as a form of agricultural organization. What are the advantages and disadvantages of the system? Why was this system created and put into practice?

children.title: 10/28-10/31- Step 3: Petition for Land
Step 3: Petition for Land

assignmentDetails.description:
Write a petition to the Mexican government to allow you to bring colonists to Texas.



Petition for Land Grant

Now that you know where you want your colony to be, you need to write a petition to the Mexican government.  Your petition must include:

  • What is your name, where are you from, what did you do before/ your previous job?

  • What characteristics do you have that would make you a good empresario? Ex: Leadership Skills, Communication Skills, Knowledge of Mexico & Laws

  • Who are you bringing with you? What types of people will you have in your colony? How will they benefit the colony and Mexico?  What qualities will your colonists have?

  • Where is your colony located?(Be specific. What rivers, lakes, and natural landmarks is it near?)  Why did you choose that location? (Refer back to Step 2)

  • How will your colony benefit Mexico?

 

Remember, you need to convince the Mexican government that they should grant your petition. Be sure to get approval from the Mexican government before you continue to the next step.

children.title: 11/01-11/03- Step 4: Colony Ad
Step 4: Colony Ad

assignmentDetails.description:
Create an advertisement that would make someone want to leave their perfectly good situation to head to Texas. The advertisement must be easy to read, straight to the point, and grab the reader's attention.

Keep in mind that you are asking a person skilled in an occupation to come somewhere new. Be sure to refer back to the Colonization Law and your notes for information.

You may complete this by hand or electronically. Electronic projects must be linked to this document or attached in Schoology.

Include:
Land Policy for colonists
Requirements of colonists
Description of Land in Texas
Location of your colony
Cost of land & payment for colonists

Ideas for electronic advertisements:
Google Slides or Google Draw
S’more

children.title: Divided Human Essay DUE 9/8

assignmentDetails.description:
Prompt: Choose one of the Native Texan tribes discussed in class (Karankawa, Caddo, Comanche, Jumano), and write 2 paragraphs describing their culture.  You may choose to be a reporter that is reporting about the tribe (expository essay), or you may choose to write a diary/ journal entries or a “day in the life” (personal narrative essay).  You must write your essay on notebook paper. You must include the following information in your essay:

  • Name of Tribe-

  • Culture Group--

  • Type of Shelter

  • Nomadic or Sedentary-

  • 2 Examples of food, and how they get their food (hunter-gatherers, farmer, both)--

  • At least 2 examples of general culture traits discussed in class (clothing, ceremonies, unique traits, etc.)

  • Description of the physical geography of the region they live

Texas Regions Maps DUE:  Wednesday, 8/28
children.content:
Texas Regions Map 

You will be drawing pictures to represent the important information for each region.

Label all 4 regions and color each one a different color.

Bodies of Water 

● Gulf of Mexico,  Rivers: Red, Rio Grande, Brazos, and Sabine 

Landforms 

● 2 landforms in each region (mountains, deserts, etc.) 

Vegetation 

● 2 picture in each region that represents the vegetation 

Climate 

● 1 picture in each region that represent the climate 

Major Cities 

● All major cities labeled (see notes) 

Economic Activities/Industries 

●  2 pictures per region that represent economic activities
